headline: High: Prefect can orchestrate actions from Opik outputs, creating default-path cascading errors and potential data leakage via broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Opik has broad network egress and REST API output surfaces, while Prefect is an orchestration system that can consume upstream outputs. No shared channel is documented, so a direct injection path is not proven; however, if Opik output is manually or programmatically fed into Prefect task inputs, prompt-like content could influence downstream automation.
conditions: IF Opik outputs are copied into Prefect task parameters or flow inputs without sanitization, injection becomes possible.
IF Prefect parses Opik-generated text as instructions, downstream task behavior can be altered.
mitigations: Add a fixed schema for Opik-to-Prefect handoff.
Strip instruction-like text before passing outputs onward.
Require human review for any free-text field.
Log and diff all upstream payloads before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Prefect touches workflow metadata by default. Opik is an observability/evaluation system that may emit run content through REST APIs. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can leak metadata or payloads if Opik outputs are forwarded into Prefect-managed workflows.
conditions: IF Opik run content is included in Prefect workflow metadata, that data can be transmitted off-host.
IF either agent is configured to send payloads to external APIs, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Minimize fields forwarded from Opik to Prefect.
Redact secrets and identifiers before orchestration.
Disable verbose run metadata where possible.
Use allowlists for outbound destinations.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Opik exposes REST API calls and Prefect calls GitHub APIs, but neither profile shows unrestricted filesystem writes, shared mutable storage, or overlapping OAuth scopes. The main overlap is read/egress behavior, so write-write conflict is not evidenced and the interaction appears limited.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same repository or directory, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free mutable state, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Keep each agent on separate workspaces.
Avoid granting write scopes unless needed.
Serialize any shared updates through one coordinator.
Add optimistic-lock checks for mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an orchestration/pipeline agent, so it can act on upstream outputs. Opik produces evaluation/observability outputs that Prefect could treat as authoritative if wired directly into a flow. Because no verification step is documented, the pair supports a default-path cascade from Opik-generated content into Prefect actions.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Opik outputs as task inputs without validation, errors can propagate.
IF Opik emits incorrect evaluation metadata, Prefect may automate the mistake.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents.
Require typed outputs from Opik.
Have Prefect reject unstructured text for control decisions.
Add a human approval gate for high-impact actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Opik is an observability tool and Prefect handles workflow metadata, so both can touch operational data classes. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles, and both are open-source with no stated secrets handling. The compliance risk is therefore limited to policy gaps if the operator routes regulated metadata through them.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in workflow metadata, retention policy mismatch becomes relevant.
IF either deployment sends data to a region or vendor outside policy, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent.
Exclude regulated fields from workflow metadata.
Set explicit retention limits in the orchestrator.
Document residency and deletion handling.
